newsitem.title: FRANCE: GEC-Alsthom in joint bid for Westinghouse unit-paper.
newsitem.headline: GEC-Alsthom in joint bid for Westinghouse unit-paper.

text.p: GEC Alsthom is looking to buy US group Westinghouse's energy divisions with the help of French state-controlled nuclear energy group Framatome, French daily Liberation said on Tuesday.

The paper said that GEC Alsthom, a joint venture between Britain's General Electric Co. Plc and French engineering and telecoms group Alcatel Alsthom, had lodged a joint bid with Framatome on July 25.
Officials at Alcatel Alsthom and Framatome, 44 percent owned by Alcatel, were not immediately available for comment.

Liberation carried photocopies of what it said were working documents for a bid by GEC Alsthom and Framatome for the Westinghouse division, which it said comprises 80 nuclear centres. Liberation said the division was worth between $1.47 and $1.55 billion.
The papers said that on July 7, a French delegation led by Pierre Bilger, head of GEC Alsthom, had met Westinghouse executives in the United States.
The US group plans to split its media and industrial operations into separate companies in September this year.
Liberation quoted a source close to the talks as saying that Framatome, which has funds of 10 billion francs, would take on the nuclear risk, estimated at between 750 and 900 million dollars.
It said the cost of the deal would be between zero and $300 million after the risk and debts had been taken into account.
